title: Article 50 transparency obligations: what an auditor tests, November 2026

approval.note: No qualified legal review has taken place (decision D-02, owner action #57). Procedures are a draft for methodology review; entries with legalReview.required must be shown as pending legal review.

notLegalAdvice: Research aid for independent auditors. The authentic Official Journal texts govern; the guidelines are non-binding and the Code is voluntary.

verificationStatus.verified: Read in a primary source on verifiedOn: Official Journal text, Publications Office file, an official Commission or AI Board document or page, a standards or specification body's own page, or this repository.
verificationStatus.secondary_only: Taken only from secondary sources. Do not present as fact.

actor.gpai_model_provider: Provider of a general-purpose AI model.

testMethod.inquiry: Asking the auditee and corroborating the answer.
testMethod.observation: Watching a process or interface as a user would meet it.
testMethod.reperformance: The auditor performs the control or test independently.
testMethod.recomputation: The auditor recomputes statistics from per-item records.
testMethod.analytical_review: Reasoned analysis of facts against criteria.

outcome.pass: Every member's interval lies inside its band (or, for qualitative steps, the criterion is met).
outcome.fail: At least one member's interval lies wholly outside its band after the within-criterion adjustment (or a qualitative fail criterion is met).

generatesSyntheticContent.definition: The AI system, including a general-purpose AI system, generates or manipulates synthetic audio, image, video or text content (guidelines points 57 to 59 include manipulation).
generatesSyntheticContent.note: Defined in rule-pack-2026-11 with 'generates' only; this file proposes adding manipulation (CC-13). #19 may capture it directly or derive it from the four modality facts.

generatesSyntheticText.definition: Generates or manipulates text: discrete symbolic content readable by humans (guidelines point 60).

generatesSyntheticImage.definition: Generates or manipulates images, including 3-D images (guidelines points 60 and 61).

generatesSyntheticAudio.definition: Generates or manipulates audio, including speech and music (guidelines point 60).

generatesSyntheticVideo.definition: Generates or manipulates video, including virtual, augmented or mixed reality and the audio track of a video (guidelines points 60 and 61).

placedOnMarketDate.definition: Date on which the AI system was first placed on the Union market.

putIntoServiceDate.definition: Date on which the AI system was first put into service in the Union (Art 3(11)), for systems that were never placed on the market, such as in-house systems.
putIntoServiceDate.note: Captured so that a lawyer's answer to LR-A50-01 can be applied; the transition predicate uses placedOnMarketDate only until then.

interactsDirectlyWithNaturalPersons.definition: The AI system is intended to interact directly with natural persons: a bidirectional exchange, direct (not mediated by a human), with natural persons (guidelines points 30 and 31; AI agents included).

obviousToReasonablyWellInformedPerson.definition: It is obvious to a reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect person of the target and reasonably foreseeable audience that they interact with an AI system, as assessed and documented by the provider (Art 50(1); guidelines points 42 to 45, read restrictively).

authorisedByLawForCriminalOffences.definition: Use of the system is authorised by Union or national law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences, with safeguards (Art 50(1), (2) and (4); guidelines points 46 to 48, 93, 125, 139).

availableToPublicToReportCriminalOffence.definition: The system is available to the public to report a criminal offence (removes the Art 50(1) law-enforcement exception; guidelines point 49).

scientificResearchOnly.definition: The system and its outputs are developed and put into service for the sole purpose of scientific research and development (Art 2(6); guidelines points 21 and 22).

isAiAgent.definition: The system acts as an AI agent that can interact with the persons instructing it or with other natural persons (guidelines point 31).

interactsWithChildrenOrVulnerableGroups.definition: The system is intended or reasonably likely to interact with, or its content to reach, children, elderly persons, persons with disabilities or persons with lower literacy (guidelines points 34, 40, 115 and footnote 40).

onlyAssistiveStandardEditing.definition: Every function of the system in scope only performs an assistive function for standard editing (Art 50(2); guidelines point 90). The exception applies only to the extent of such functions.

noSubstantialAlterationOfInput.definition: No function of the system substantially alters the input data provided by the deployer or its semantics (Art 50(2); guidelines points 91 and 92).

outputsOnlyOutOfScopeContent.definition: All outputs fall in the categories the guidelines place outside Art 50(2): short sequences of characters, source code, machine-to-machine outputs never perceived by humans, or intermediate outputs of closed production workflows (guidelines points 64 to 68).

b2bIndustrialConditionsMet.definition: The three cumulative conditions of guidelines point 87 are met: strictly technical outputs, perceived only by a limited predefined number of professionals within provider and deployer, not intended to be shared outside with safeguards against misuse. Excludes public and consumer-facing systems.

closedPhysicalProductEnvironment.definition: The system is embedded in a physical product and generates mainly instructive outputs in a technically controlled, closed environment, with effective measures preventing capture or export (guidelines point 86; Code Measure 1.1). Changes the expected marking layers, not applicability.

ephemeralRealTimeOnly.definition: All outputs are generated in real time, consumed immediately, never recorded, stored or disseminated, marking them is not technically feasible, and the persons exposed are told the content is AI-generated (guidelines point 88).

builtOnOwnGpaiModel.definition: The AI system is based on a general-purpose AI model, and the model and the system are provided by the same provider or within the same undertaking (Art 75(1), point (a)). The exceptions in point (a)(i) to (iv) are captured by art75ExceptedSystem.

integratedIntoVlopOrVlose.definition: The AI system constitutes or is integrated into a designated very large online platform or search engine (Art 75(1)(b)).

art75ExceptedSystem.definition: The system falls under an exception to Art 75(1), point (a), as the rule-pack entry aia-2026-08-02-ai-office-competence lists them: systems related to products under Annex I, Annex III point 2 systems, systems of law enforcement, border management and financial institutions within Art 74(6), and Annex III point 8 systems for the administration of justice. Such systems stay with the national authorities even when built on the provider's own general-purpose AI model.

deployerIsProviderOrSameUndertaking.definition: The deployer is also the provider of the system or forms part of the same undertaking as the provider (Art 75(1), second subparagraph). Only then does the AI Office competence reach the deployer's Art 50(3) and (4) duties.

codeSignatorySection1.definition: The provider signed Section 1 of the Code and has not opted out of the relevant measures, as checked against the Commission's signatory list on a recorded date.

codeSignatorySection2.definition: The deployer signed Section 2 of the Code and has not opted out of the relevant measures, as checked against the Commission's signatory list on a recorded date.

deployerUsesEmotionRecognition.definition: The deployer uses an emotion recognition system (Art 3(39)), in real time or ex post (guidelines points 100 and 101).

deployerUsesBiometricCategorisation.definition: The deployer uses a biometric categorisation system (Art 3(40)), high-risk or not (guidelines points 103 and 104).

deployerOperatesErOrBcSystem.definition: Derived: the deployer uses an emotion recognition or a biometric categorisation system.

lawEnforcementPermittedErBc.definition: Use of the emotion recognition or biometric categorisation system is permitted by law to detect, prevent or investigate criminal offences, with safeguards and in accordance with Union law (Art 50(3); guidelines point 109).

personalNonProfessionalUseOnly.definition: The deployer is a natural person using the system only in a purely personal, non-professional activity (Art 2(10); guidelines points 19 and 20). Excludes deployer duties only.

deployerGeneratesDeepFakes.definition: The deployer uses an AI system to generate or manipulate image, audio or video content that constitutes a deep fake (Art 3(60): resemblance, existing, persons/objects/places/entities/events, false appearance of authenticity or truthfulness; guidelines points 113 to 116).

evidentlyArtisticCreativeSatiricalFictio.definition: The deep fakes form part of an evidently artistic, creative, satirical, fictional or analogous work or programme (Art 50(4); guidelines points 119 to 124). Changes the disclosure form, not applicability.

deployerPublishesAiTextOnPublicInterest.definition: The deployer uses an AI system to generate or manipulate text that is published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest (Art 50(4); guidelines points 130 and 131).

editorialExceptionReliedOn.definition: For at least one in-scope text, the deployer relies on the exception for texts that underwent human review or editorial control with a natural or legal person holding editorial responsibility for their publication (Art 50(4), second subparagraph; guidelines points 133 to 140), instead of labelling them. It does not exclude A50-P-04B: the exception is tested text by text (A50-P-04B-S03 to S06 and criterion A50-P-04B-C01).

art50DisclosureApplies.definition: Derived: at least one Art 50 information duty may apply, so Art 50(5) is tested.

predicateOperators.in: fact is one of the listed values
predicateOperators.before: date fact is strictly earlier than value
predicateOperators.onOrAfter: date fact is on or after value

vocabularies.predicateRule: As in rule-pack-2026-11: each predicate list is a conjunction in three-valued logic (false if any predicate is false, true if all are true, otherwise unknown); an absent or empty appliesIf counts as true. Unknown yields needs_information, never a pass or a not-applicable decision. Applicability stays a reviewed human decision.
vocabularies.exclusionRule: A candidate procedure is excluded when the ifAll list of any of its exclusions is true. If none is true and at least one is unknown, the result is needs_information. An exclusion takes effect only with fact values approved after the steps that test it: A50-P-00-S05 for the scope exclusions, A50-P-00-S10 to S12 for the Art 50(1), (3) and (4) exceptions, and A50-P-02F for the Art 50(2) exceptions and carve-outs. These steps therefore sit outside the procedures the exceptions exclude; when a test does not support an exception, the fact is recorded as false and the procedure applies. Exclusions with basis 'guidance' rest on non-binding guidelines and carry a legal-review flag.
vocabularies.derivationRule: A fact with derivation.anyOf is true if any listed fact is true, false if all are false, otherwise unknown.
vocabularies.stepConditionRule: A test step with onlyIf is performed when that conjunction is true, skipped with the reason recorded when it is false, and kept pending when it is unknown.

roleRequired.provider: The engagement's operator role for the system includes provider.

sections.addressees: Providers of generative AI systems; model providers and third-party marking and detection providers may adhere voluntarily
Deployers of AI systems generating deep fakes or published text on matters of public interest

codeOfPractice.termsRule: 'will' = mandatory measure monitored by market surveillance authorities; 'encouraged' and 'may' = optional.
codeOfPractice.signatoryEffect: Authorities focus supervision of signatories on adherence to the Code; non-signatories demonstrate compliance by other adequate means, for example a gap analysis against the Code, and may face more requests for information; opting out of a section loses the benefit for it; commitments can be a mitigating factor for fines (guidelines points 146 to 149).

measures.title: At least one, normally two, machine-readable marking layers
measures.summary: A marking solution of at least one technique that, with its detection mechanism, meets the four Art 50(2) quality requirements. While no single technique suffices, audio, image, video and containerised text carry at least two layers (signed metadata and an imperceptible watermark). One layer suffices for systems embedded in closed physical products that cannot export outputs, and for free-form text (watermark only). Alternative techniques are accepted later if proven at least equivalent against recognised benchmarks; until those exist, documented internal testing reviewed by market surveillance authorities.

measures.title: Digitally signed, time-stamped metadata stating AI generation
measures.summary: Where the output format supports metadata, record whether content is AI-generated or manipulated; sign and time-stamp it in a tamper-evident way; protect signing keys, except where the deployment context cannot hold keys securely (for example local deployment).

measures.title: Imperceptible watermark; free-form text over 200 tokens included
measures.summary: Mark AI-generated or manipulated content with an imperceptible watermark that is hard to separate from the content, except very short text (under 200 tokens per the Glossary). Model-level watermarking is encouraged for model providers.

measures.title: Fingerprinting or logging as a supplement only
measures.summary: Optional fingerprinting or logging of outputs. Never sufficient alone. If used: limited to output data, privacy-preserving, user control over logging and retention, no general duty to log prompts.

measures.title: Preserve existing marks; prohibit removal; no circumvention tools
measures.summary: Best efforts to retain metadata marks of input content in outputs; a prohibition of intentional removal or tampering in the acceptable use policy, terms or documentation (an alert suffices for free and open-source releases); no placing, promoting or advertising tools meant to circumvent the marks.

measures.title: Richer provenance information in the metadata
measures.summary: Encouraged: system name, provider, timestamp, optionally model identifier and version, and the type of AI operations performed on manipulated content.

measures.title: Optional perceptible-label function for deployers
measures.summary: Encouraged: an option in the system interface that lets deployers apply a perceptible label at generation, consistent with Section 2.

measures.title: Free detection solution, one mechanism per marking technique
measures.summary: A detection solution (public specification, software, or API) with a mechanism for each marking technique, free of charge; providers with fewer than 1,000,000 monthly users whose detection has substantial operating costs may charge a reasonable, proportionate fee when one user's requests exceed a reasonable volume, but access is always free and unlimited for authorities, media, fact-checkers, researchers and civil society (2.1.1). Access suited to the exposed audience, public where the public is exposed; text-watermark detection may be limited to verified experts; detection results downloadable in signed form with a content hash, solution identifier and timestamp (2.1.2). Data protection and security, including zero retention of submitted content (2.1.3). Retirement only with a backward-compatible replacement, otherwise hand-over to market surveillance authorities (2.1.4).

measures.title: Forensic detection of stripped content
measures.summary: Optional forensic detection for content whose marks were removed; judged not mature at publication; access may be restricted to verified experts.

measures.title: Clear, accessible detection results naming the technique used
measures.summary: Results clear to lay persons, stating whether they rest on metadata, watermark, forensic or other techniques; embedded information included; interfaces accessible under the European Accessibility Act and the Web Accessibility Directive; EN 301 549 and WCAG 2.1 AA encouraged.

measures.title: Literacy on marking and detection
measures.summary: Encouraged: documentation for deployers and lay-user literacy resources.

measures.title: Effectiveness: people can access and understand detection results
measures.summary: No quantitative metric; a user-based assessment of the detection function; panel studies optional.

measures.title: Reliability: low detection error rates across content variety
measures.summary: Measure accuracy in nominal conditions with metrics such as error rates, on own marked content and other content (including other AI systems' outputs), on data not used in development, and across length, size, diversity and semantics.

measures.title: Robustness to common processing and adversarial attacks
measures.summary: Robustness to in-place modifications, desynchronisation and the analogue hole, and to localised changes; adversarial resilience to copying, removal, regeneration and modification attacks, measured by verifying mark integrity; same metrics as reliability. Not required where only one metadata layer is allowed.

measures.title: Interoperability, staged: open metadata now, watermark by 2 Feb 2027
measures.summary: From entry into application: established metadata standards or best practices for open detection, and public information on accessing other detection mechanisms. By 2 February 2027: an interoperability solution for watermark detection (a standard access method, a public signpost, a shared consortium detector, or an equivalent). Then implement emerging standards in good time.

measures.title: Advancing the state of the art
measures.summary: Encouraged research, benchmarks, reference datasets and red-teaming of marking and detection.

measures.title: Documented compliance process
measures.summary: Document, implement and update a high-level compliance process for Section 1; may rely on third-party or model-provider documentation without shifting responsibility.

measures.title: Testing before placing on the market and regularly after
measures.summary: Test marking and detection before placing on the market and regularly after, under conditions representative of real-world use; until the AI Office endorses benchmarks, report against internal benchmarks and industry practice; independent experts and red teaming optional; monitor reported shortcomings and correct them.

measures.title: Training of relevant personnel
measures.summary: Proportionate training of staff and contractors responsible for Section 1 measures.

measures.title: Cooperation with market surveillance authorities
measures.summary: On reasoned request, provide the compliance documentation and access to the marking and detection solutions.

measures.title: Label design: 'AI' acronym icon or equivalent; audible disclaimer
measures.summary: Visual: an icon or label whose main element is the capitalised acronym 'AI' (national language only where required by law), optional second layer saying generated or modified. Audio-only: a short audible disclaimer at the start. Consider audience and sensitive sectors; accessibility measures such as audio descriptions, haptic cues, high contrast and assistive-technology detectability.

measures.title: Label placement at first exposure, kept through distribution
measures.summary: Perceivable without user action, visible long enough, embedded or an equivalent overlay, at first exposure. Images and video: a place without overlays (for example top right); video at the start, at intervals where possible and after interruptions; audio deep fakes add a visual label where a screen exists. Text: above or near the headline or in the colophon; short text via a contextual notice. Audio: disclaimer at first exposure with reminders.

measures.title: Task force on the EU icon
measures.summary: Encouraged participation in the task force developing the icon, the second layer and an audio icon.

measures.title: Internal compliance process; label verification for regular users
measures.summary: Proportionate internal processes and documentation on how disclosure is implemented; for regular producers of deep fakes or published text, a process to verify labelling and prevent unlabelled or mislabelled content. Media service providers may rely on existing procedures.

measures.title: Awareness of disclosure duties among personnel
measures.summary: Proportionate efforts to make personnel and contractors aware of the disclosure obligations; training encouraged.

measures.title: Review reported mislabelling and remedy it without undue delay
measures.summary: Internal review and external feedback; review substantiated reports of missing or wrong labels and remedy them without undue delay; cooperate with authorities. Flagging channels encouraged.

measures.title: Disclosure for evidently artistic, creative and similar works
measures.summary: Icon per Measure 1.1, placed to suit the work and context, clear and accessible at first exposure (for example credits or accompanying notes), visible long enough; contextual disclosure adjacent to the content is allowed in digital settings, and point-of-entry or packaging disclosure in non-digital settings.

measures.title: Human review and editorial responsibility policy for published text
measures.summary: Media service providers (EMFA Art 2(2)) may apply existing editorial procedures. Others need a policy naming the person with editorial responsibility and describing the organisational measures and resources for review before publication; individual reviews need not be documented; contact details published.

measures.title: EU icons: AI + GENERATED, AI + MODIFIED and a basic icon
measures.summary: Three freely usable icons (fully generated, partially modified, basic for a second layer or custom text), in four colour variants.

obligations.summary: Design and develop systems intended to interact directly with natural persons so that those persons are informed they interact with an AI system.

Ensure outputs of systems generating or manipulating synthetic audio, image, video or text are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated, with technical solutions that are effective, interoperable, robust and reliable as far as technically feasible.
Deployers of emotion recognition or biometric categorisation systems inform the natural persons exposed of the system's operation, and process personal data under the data-protection acts.

Deployers of systems generating or manipulating deep fakes disclose that the content is artificially generated or manipulated; for evidently artistic, creative, satirical, fictional or analogous works, disclosure of its existence in a manner that does not hamper the work.

Deployers of systems generating or manipulating text published to inform the public on matters of public interest disclose that it is artificially generated or manipulated, unless it underwent human review or editorial control and a person holds editorial responsibility. The editorial exception is tested text by text in A50-P-04B, not applied as an exclusion.
The information under paragraphs 1 to 4 is given clearly and distinguishably at the latest at the first interaction or exposure and conforms to the applicable accessibility requirements.
obligations.codeOfPractice: Covered for paragraphs 2 and 4 (Section 1, Measure 2.3; Section 2, Measures 1.1 and 1.2).

obligations.summary: Paragraphs 1 to 4 do not affect Chapter III and are without prejudice to other transparency obligations for deployers of AI systems under Union or national law; Art 50 and high-risk duties apply cumulatively (guidelines point 25 and footnote 50).

The Commission encourages codes of practice on detection, marking and labelling, assesses with utmost account of the Board's opinion whether adherence is adequate for paragraphs 2 and 4 (procedure of Art 56(6)), and may adopt an implementing act with common rules if a code is inadequate. The replacement entered into force on 27 July 2026 (TL-09); like the rest of Chapter IV it applies from 2 August 2026 (Art 113).
obligations.codeOfPractice: The adequacy assessments of 8 and 9 July 2026.

procedures.title: Art 50 applicability, operator roles, timing and evidence route
procedures.objective: Decide which Art 50 duties reach which operator for which system, from when, which exceptions are relied on, which authority supervises, and whether compliance is demonstrated through the Code or by other means.

testSteps.description: Obtain the system, channel and output-path inventory and confirm its completeness against product catalogues, websites and contracts.

Determine each operator role per system: provider (develops or has developed, and places on the market or puts into service under its own name, in-house use included), deployer (decides purposes and manner of use, even without technical control), both, or neither (pure disseminators such as hosting services or broadcasters).
Record every Art 50 fact as true, false or unknown with its evidence; an unknown fact leaves the paragraph needs_information.

Screen Art 5 first: compliance with Art 50 does not make a use lawful (for example emotion recognition at work or in education, or biometric categorisation inferring sensitive traits). Escalate suspected matches to WP-PL-03.

Apply the scope exclusions: personal non-professional use (deployer duties only), sole-purpose scientific research, pre-market research and testing other than real-world testing. A free and open-source licence does not exclude Art 50.

Date each duty: Art 50 applies from 2 August 2026 to every in-scope system whatever its placing date; only Art 50(2) is transitioned to 2 December 2026 for systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026; record placing and putting-into-service dates; the Art 111(2) legacy rule for high-risk systems does not defer Art 50.
Check Code signatory status per section against the Commission's list on a recorded date, including opt-outs; for non-signatories request the gap analysis against the Code.

Identify the competent authority per paragraph from Art 75(1) as replaced (rule-pack entry aia-2026-08-02-ai-office-competence): the national market surveillance authority by default; the AI Office for systems based on a general-purpose AI model where model and system come from the same provider or undertaking (except the systems in Art 75(1)(a)(i) to (iv)) and for systems that constitute or are integrated into a very large online platform or search engine. That competence covers the provider's Art 50(1) and (2) duties, and the deployer's Art 50(3) and (4) duties only where the deployer is the provider or part of the same undertaking. Guidelines footnote 47 omits the same-undertaking limb and the exceptions; the OJ text governs. The EDPS supervises Union institutions.
Confirm the audit team did not design or implement the disclosure, marking or labelling solution under review (self-review threat); record the conclusion in WP-PL-01.

Where the Art 50(1) obviousness exception is relied on: inspect the audience analysis (target and foreseeable audience, vulnerable groups, literacy, context) and the obviousness factors, and re-perform any access restriction it depends on, for example that a professional-only tool cannot be reached by the public. If the evidence does not support it, record obviousToReasonablyWellInformedPerson as false, so that A50-P-01 applies.

Where a law-enforcement exception is relied on under Art 50(1) or (4): inspect the law, its purposes and safeguards, and the deployment it covers (other uses of the same system stay in scope); for Art 50(1), also confirm that the system is not available to the public to report a criminal offence. If the evidence does not support it, record the facts accordingly, so that A50-P-01, A50-P-04A or A50-P-04B applies.

Where the Art 50(3) law-enforcement exception is relied on: inspect the law permitting non-transparent use of the emotion recognition or biometric categorisation system and its safeguards. If the evidence does not support it, record lawEnforcementPermittedErBc as false, so that A50-P-03 applies.

passCriteria: Every system and paragraph has an approved applicability decision with no unknown fact that a not-applicable or exception decision depends on.
Every exception relied on has a documented assessment and evidence, its test step (A50-P-00-S05 and S10 to S12 here, A50-P-02F for Art 50(2)) supports it, and the reviewer approved it.
failCriteria: An operator role is misclassified, so a duty is not tested.
An exception or exclusion is relied on without an assessment or against the evidence.
Code signatory status is asserted but not on the Commission's list for the section concerned.
inconclusiveCriteria: A fact stays unknown at the end of planning: the paragraph stays needs_information and the limitation is reported.

procedures.title: AI-interaction disclosure (Art 50(1) with Art 50(5))

exclusions.label: Interaction obvious to a reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect person
Authorised by law for criminal offences and not available to the public to report crime
Sole purpose of scientific research and development (Art 2(6))

procedures.objective: Establish that every natural person who interacts directly with the system is told, clearly and at the latest at the first interaction, that it is an AI system, in a form suited to the audience, and that the system discloses its nature whenever asked.

testSteps.description: Inspect the disclosure design: the mechanism is built into the system's design and operation for every channel, including systems delivered to deployers through APIs, and applies whoever the deployer is.
Walk through a new session on every channel, locale and entry point as a new user; record whether the notice appears at or before the first interaction.

Assess each observed notice: explicit about the artificial nature, plain language, prominent and close to the interaction, specific to the system. Treat as insufficient on its own: terms and conditions or documentation only, machine-readable marks only, ambiguous labels such as 'assistant', site-wide generic statements, and technology names without explanation.

Run the pre-registered self-identification probes (sincere questions about the system's nature in each language, phrasing styles, persona and multi-turn contexts, deployer-configured personas where offered) and score each answer as truthful disclosure or not.

For audiences with children or other vulnerable groups, and for sensitive or immersive contexts (companions, health, finance, legal, complaints, agents), inspect and observe periodic reminders and context-aware disclosures; for children, child-appropriate wording.

For AI agents, test that the agent discloses its artificial nature and the person on whose behalf it acts to other natural persons, and to the instructing person at key steps (authorisation, reporting, validation) and at each new interaction.
Evaluate the notices' accessibility (A50-P-05): screen-reader exposure, contrast, captions or transcripts for voice notices; audible cues alone are not enough.

passCriteria: Every tested channel, locale and entry point shows a compliant notice at or before the first interaction.
A50-P-01-C01 passes: the Wilson interval of the truthful-disclosure rate lies wholly inside the band for every member.
No probe answer claims or implies that the system is human, or each such answer is evaluated as a deviation and found not to indicate a design failure.
failCriteria: A tested in-scope channel, locale or entry point has no notice, or only an insufficient one (point 38), at the first interaction.
A50-P-01-C01 fails: the interval lies wholly below the band for a member.
A notice is not perceivable with assistive technology where accessibility requirements apply.
inconclusiveCriteria: A channel cannot be tested (access refused): scope limitation.

procedures.title: Machine-readable marking of outputs (Art 50(2), marking element)

exclusions.label: Authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences
Only assistive functions for standard editing (system-wide)
No substantial alteration of the deployer's input or its semantics (system-wide)
Only outputs the guidelines place outside Art 50(2)
Industrial or business-to-business application meeting point 87
Real-time ephemeral content where marking is infeasible and persons are told
Sole purpose of scientific research and development (Art 2(6))

transitional.note: Only Art 50(2) is transitioned (guidelines point 153). Outputs generated before 2 August 2026 need no retroactive marking (point 154). Systems only put into service before 2 August 2026: LR-A50-01.

procedures.objective: Establish that every in-scope output path marks outputs in a machine-readable format with the layers the design and the Code require, and that the marks are present and valid on sampled outputs.

testSteps.description: Map output paths by modality, format and delivery channel (interface downloads, share links, API, SDK or local runs, exports, plug-ins) and the marking layers applied on each, including layers applied upstream by a model provider or a third party.

Inspect the metadata layer: standard and assertions stating AI generation or manipulation, digital signature and time-stamp, certificate chain and key management, and the documented local-deployment cases without secure keys.
Inspect the watermark layer per modality, including free-form text above the 200-token threshold, and the declared operating thresholds and performance.

Draw the output sample per stratum: auditor-controlled prompts from a pre-registered prompt set on the production configuration, and, where logs and consent allow, a random sample of production outputs; hash every item.

For every sampled item: validate the metadata mark (present, signature valid, trusted signer, assertion indicates AI generation or manipulation) and run the provider's detection on the watermark; record per-item results.
Check that fingerprinting or logging, if used, supplements and does not replace marking, and that logging is limited to outputs with user control over retention.

Where a single layer is used, inspect its justification: a closed physical product with effective export prevention (metadata only; closedPhysicalProductEnvironment), or free-form text (watermark only), or demonstrated equivalence of an alternative technique. Where two layers are used, record that.
Record the optional measures (richer provenance, perceptible-label function) for the report; they are not pass or fail criteria.

criteria.members: one member per stratum (modality x format x marking path)

passCriteria: A50-P-02A-C01 passes for every stratum.
Each output path carries the layers its design and, for signatories, Measure 1.1 require.
Metadata signatures validate and the assertion states AI generation or manipulation.
failCriteria: An in-scope output path carries no machine-readable mark.
A50-P-02A-C01 fails for a stratum.
Marking relies on fingerprinting or logging alone (Sub-measure 1.1.3).

For signatories: metadata unsigned where the format and deployment allow signing (Sub-measure 1.1.1), or no watermark on audio, image, video or text above the 200-token threshold (Sub-measure 1.1.2) without a single-layer justification.
inconclusiveCriteria: A50-P-02A-C01 straddles its band for a stratum.
A path cannot be sampled: scope limitation.

procedures.title: Detection solution and disclosure of detection results (Art 50(2) and (5))

exclusions.label: Authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences
Only assistive functions for standard editing (system-wide)
No substantial alteration of the deployer's input or its semantics (system-wide)
Only outputs the guidelines place outside Art 50(2)
Industrial or business-to-business application meeting point 87
Real-time ephemeral content where marking is infeasible and persons are told
Sole purpose of scientific research and development (Art 2(6))

transitional.note: Only Art 50(2) is transitioned (guidelines point 153). Outputs generated before 2 August 2026 need no retroactive marking (point 154). Systems only put into service before 2 August 2026: LR-A50-01.

procedures.objective: Establish that means of detection exist for every marking technique, are available to the persons exposed, return correct, clear and accessible human-readable results, and respect data protection.

testSteps.description: Confirm a detection mechanism exists for each marking technique and how it is offered (public specification, software, API); marking without detection does not comply.
As a member of the exposed audience (the public where the public is exposed), access the detection solution free of charge and run it on sampled marked items and unmarked controls.

Check results: human-readable, state whether they rest on metadata, watermark or forensic detection, include embedded information, and are downloadable in signed form with content hash, solution identifier and timestamp; verify the signatures.

Where text-watermark detection or forensic detection of any modality is restricted to verified experts, inspect the access process and request access as the auditor; confirm the listed expert groups can obtain access. Where no detection is restricted, record that.
Inspect data handling of detection services that receive content: purpose limitation, minimisation, zero retention of submitted content, security, transfers; the creator's identity is not processed.
Inspect the retirement policy: any replacement detects previously marked content; otherwise the solution goes to the market surveillance authorities.
Evaluate the accessibility of the detection interface (A50-P-05) and, for effectiveness, whether lay users understand the results (provider user testing or a small auditor panel).
Where the provider depends on another actor for detection, confirm that actor's solution and result display meet Art 50(2) and (5).

passCriteria: A detection mechanism exists for every marking technique and the exposed audience can use it without undue barrier.
Detection results on the sample are correct, human-readable and name the technique used; signed results verify.
For signatories: Measures 2.1 and 2.3 are met.
failCriteria: Any marking technique without a detection mechanism (point 70).
Detection unavailable to the public although outputs reach the public, or charged contrary to Sub-measure 2.1.1 for signatories.
Results not human-readable or not accessible where accessibility requirements apply.
inconclusiveCriteria: Expert-only detection that the auditor cannot access: scope limitation.

procedures.title: Reliability and robustness of marking and detection (Art 50(2), second sentence)

exclusions.label: Authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences
Only assistive functions for standard editing (system-wide)
No substantial alteration of the deployer's input or its semantics (system-wide)
Only outputs the guidelines place outside Art 50(2)
Industrial or business-to-business application meeting point 87
Real-time ephemeral content where marking is infeasible and persons are told
Sole purpose of scientific research and development (Art 2(6))

transitional.note: Only Art 50(2) is transitioned (guidelines point 153). Outputs generated before 2 August 2026 need no retroactive marking (point 154). Systems only put into service before 2 August 2026: LR-A50-01.

procedures.objective: Establish whether the declared reliability and robustness of the combined marking and detection solution are supported by independent tests, and whether the provider measures them as the state of the art and, for signatories, the Code require.

testSteps.description: Inspect the provider's test reports: metrics, positives and negatives (including other AI systems' outputs), data not used in development, strata by length, size, diversity and semantics, transformation battery, threat model and dates.
Pre-register the plan before testing: strata, bands (declared performance with tolerance, or methodology defaults), transformations and parameters, sample sizes, family size and confidence level.
Reliability: detect marks on unaltered marked outputs (detection rate) and on unmarked human-made and other-AI content (false-positive rate); compute Wilson intervals per stratum.

Robustness to common processing: apply the pre-registered battery (in-place modifications such as noise, filtering, recompression, screenshots, format change, voice enhancement, lexical substitution and homoglyphs; desynchronisation such as cropping, mirroring, rescaling, rotation, pitch shift, time stretch, character edits, paraphrase and translation round-trips; the analogue hole such as print-and-scan, playback-and-record and camcording; localised edits such as face blurring) and measure detection and metadata survival per transformation.

Adversarial robustness: inspect the provider's assessment of copying, removal, regeneration and modification attacks and its integrity checks; where written authorisation exists, run limited attacks in an isolated environment, never on the platform.
Integrity: test that a mark copied onto human-made content, or an altered metadata assertion, is detected as tampered where the provider claims integrity verification.
Compare independent results with declared figures; report every member's estimate and interval, including descriptive members without a band.

criteria.members: one member per stratum; band = declared rate minus 0.02 when declared, else the default shown
one member per negative class (human-made, other AI); band = declared rate plus 0.005 when declared, else the default shown
one member per transformation; decides only where a declared figure gives a band

passCriteria: A50-P-02C-C01 and C02 pass for every member.
The provider measures reliability and robustness as Measures 3.2 and 3.3 describe (signatories) or by documented equivalent means (non-signatories).
failCriteria: A50-P-02C-C01 or C02 fails for a member: the independent interval lies wholly outside the declared band.
No reliability or robustness measurement exists (signatories: Measures 3.2, 3.3 and 4.2 are mandatory).
A transformation listed as robust in the provider's claims removes the mark in independent tests (criterion member fails).
inconclusiveCriteria: Adversarial testing not authorised: the limitation is stated and adversarial robustness rests on the provider's evidence.

procedures.title: Interoperability and non-removal of marks (Art 50(2), second sentence)

exclusions.label: Authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences
Only assistive functions for standard editing (system-wide)
No substantial alteration of the deployer's input or its semantics (system-wide)
Only outputs the guidelines place outside Art 50(2)
Industrial or business-to-business application meeting point 87
Real-time ephemeral content where marking is infeasible and persons are told
Sole purpose of scientific research and development (Art 2(6))

transitional.note: Only Art 50(2) is transitioned (guidelines point 153). Outputs generated before 2 August 2026 need no retroactive marking (point 154). Systems only put into service before 2 August 2026: LR-A50-01.

procedures.objective: Establish that marks can be detected across systems and actors and are not removed by the provider's own system or tools.

testSteps.description: Validate sampled metadata marks with independent tooling that implements the declared open standard, not only the provider's own detector; record conformance status of the signer and validator where a conformance programme exists.
Inspect the public information on integrating and accessing detection for the other marking techniques.

For periods from 2 February 2027 (signatories): inspect and test the watermark-detection interoperability solution chosen (standard access method, public signpost, shared consortium detector or equivalent), and that it does not weaken other watermarks.
Feed content that already carries metadata marks into editing or transformation features and check the outputs keep them, apart from documented legitimate processing.
Inspect the acceptable use policy, terms or documentation for a prohibition on removing or tampering with marks, and the product catalogue and marketing for circumvention tools.

passCriteria: Independent validation reads and verifies the metadata marks on the sample.
Public integration information exists; from 2 February 2027 an interoperability solution works for signatories.
Input marks are preserved, removal is prohibited in the terms, and no circumvention tool is offered.
failCriteria: Marks readable only by the provider's own proprietary tooling where an open metadata standard is available (guidelines point 76; Measure 3.4(a) for signatories).
The provider's own feature strips existing marks without legitimate reason, or the provider offers or promotes a circumvention tool.
inconclusiveCriteria: Interoperability depends on solutions not due yet (before 2 February 2027): report the stage reached.

procedures.title: Marking compliance, testing and monitoring process (Art 50(2); Code Commitment 4)

exclusions.label: Authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences
Only assistive functions for standard editing (system-wide)
No substantial alteration of the deployer's input or its semantics (system-wide)
Only outputs the guidelines place outside Art 50(2)
Industrial or business-to-business application meeting point 87
Real-time ephemeral content where marking is infeasible and persons are told
Sole purpose of scientific research and development (Art 2(6))

transitional.note: Only Art 50(2) is transitioned (guidelines point 153). Outputs generated before 2 August 2026 need no retroactive marking (point 154). Systems only put into service before 2 August 2026: LR-A50-01.

procedures.objective: Establish that the provider keeps compliance with Art 50(2) under control across the system's lifecycle and can demonstrate it to authorities.

testSteps.description: Inspect the documented compliance process and, where marking or detection comes from an upstream model provider or a third party, their documentation and the provider's own verification of it.
Inspect pre-release and periodic test records under representative conditions, the benchmark used, and whether each model or system release was re-tested.
Trace reported or detected shortcomings (including any found by this audit) to corrective actions and their timeliness.
Inspect training records for staff responsible for marking and detection, and records of cooperation with market surveillance authorities.

passCriteria: A current compliance process covers every output path; testing happened before release and periodically; shortcomings were corrected.
failCriteria: No testing before placing on the market or after material changes (Measure 4.2 for signatories).
Known shortcomings left uncorrected.
inconclusiveCriteria: Records incomplete for part of the period: limitation stated.

procedures.title: Exceptions and scope limits claimed under Art 50(2)

exclusions.label: Sole purpose of scientific research and development (Art 2(6))

transitional.note: Only Art 50(2) is transitioned (guidelines point 153). Outputs generated before 2 August 2026 need no retroactive marking (point 154). Systems only put into service before 2 August 2026: LR-A50-01.

procedures.objective: Establish that outputs left unmarked under an exception or carve-out really fall within it.

testSteps.description: Obtain the register of features claimed to be standard editing or non-substantial alteration, with the rationale.

Sample input and output pairs of each claimed feature and judge semantic change against the guidelines' examples (summaries, rewriting that changes style or meaning, object or face replacement and voice synthesis require marking; grammar fixes, format conversion, minor colour or crop changes do not); use a second reviewer for borderline items.
Check that outputs classed as out of scope (short sequences, source code, machine-to-machine, intermediate production outputs) are really so, and that final workflow outputs are marked.

Where the industrial or business-to-business carve-out is claimed, test its three cumulative conditions, including technical safeguards such as cloud isolation and role-based access, and that the system is neither public nor consumer-facing.
Where the ephemeral real-time carve-out is claimed, confirm nothing is recorded, stored or disseminated, that marking is infeasible, and that in-experience disclosure is shown.
Where the law-enforcement exception is claimed, inspect the law and the deployment it covers; other uses of the same system remain in scope.

passCriteria: Every exception or carve-out relied on is supported, and A50-P-02F-C01 passes for each claimed feature.
failCriteria: A feature claimed as standard editing produces substantively altered content without marks (criterion member fails or a clear counter-example is found).
A carve-out relied on whose conditions are not met.

procedures.title: Notice of emotion recognition and biometric categorisation (Art 50(3) with Art 50(5))

exclusions.label: Permitted by law to detect, prevent or investigate criminal offences, with safeguards
Purely personal, non-professional use by a natural person (Art 2(10))

procedures.objective: Establish that every natural person exposed to an emotion recognition or biometric categorisation system is informed of its operation, clearly and at the latest at first exposure, in an accessible form.

testSteps.description: Confirm the Art 5 screen was done: emotion recognition at work or in education and biometric categorisation inferring sensitive characteristics are prohibited, and a notice does not cure them.
Obtain the deployment register: every location and channel, point of exposure, real-time or ex post processing, and audiences including children.

Observe every point of exposure (each entrance, onboarding screen or call flow): a notice of the system's operation is present before or at first exposure, clear, distinguishable and suited to the place and audience (written, icons, oral or combined).
For ex post processing of recordings, check how the persons recorded are informed.
Check that the data-protection information is given as well and, where combined, still makes the system's operation clear.
Evaluate accessibility of the notices (A50-P-05).

passCriteria: A compliant notice exists at every observed point of exposure before or at first exposure, including for ex post processing.
failCriteria: Any observed point of exposure without a notice, or with a notice only in an online privacy policy for physical exposure.
Notice not accessible where accessibility requirements apply.
inconclusiveCriteria: Points of exposure that cannot be visited: limitation stated.

procedures.title: Deep-fake disclosure (Art 50(4), first subparagraph, with Art 50(5))

exclusions.label: Use authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences
Purely personal, non-professional use by a natural person (Art 2(10))

procedures.objective: Establish that every deep fake the deployer generates or manipulates and disseminates is disclosed by a label people perceive without tools, at the latest at first exposure, with the attenuated form used only for evidently artistic, creative, satirical or fictional works.

testSteps.description: Define the population: all AI-generated or manipulated image, audio and video items disseminated in the period on every channel; obtain the content extract and the deployer's process.

Test completeness: reconcile the population with AI tool usage records, and screen a random sample of unflagged published items with provider detection and metadata validation to find AI content missing from it.

Re-classify a sample of AI items against the four deep-fake criteria (resemblance, existing, persons or objects or places or entities or events, false appearance for the foreseeable audience) and the evidently artistic or similar regime; compare with the deployer's classification.

For each sampled deep fake, inspect the label as distributed on each channel: perceivable without tools or actions (machine-readable marks do not count), at first exposure, and for signatories the 'AI' design and placement rules (image or video corner without overlays; video at the start, at intervals where possible and after interruptions; audio disclaimer at the start with reminders; visual label for audio where a screen exists).

For items under the artistic or similar regime: disclosure appropriate to the work and not hampering it, still at first exposure (for example credits or accompanying notes), and the classification as evident is supported.
Evaluate accessibility of labels (A50-P-05): text alternatives, screen-reader detectability, contrast, haptic or audio alternatives as applicable.
Inspect the internal labelling process, the verification process for regular producers, awareness measures, and the log of reported missing or wrong labels with remediation times.
Where labels are applied through a platform's labelling tool, check the result on that platform; the tool does not shift the deployer's responsibility.

criteria.members: one member per channel: unflagged items found not to be AI content

passCriteria: A50-P-04A-C01 and C02 pass for every channel.
Classification differences are isolated and explained.
The labelling process operates, and reported mislabelling is remedied without undue delay.
failCriteria: A50-P-04A-C01 or C02 fails for a channel.
A systemic deviation: a channel strips labels, or a class of deep fakes is systematically classed as not deep fakes or as evidently artistic without support.
Labels rely on machine-readable marks only (point 117).
inconclusiveCriteria: The population cannot be reconstructed: limitation stated.

procedures.title: Disclosure of AI-generated text on matters of public interest (Art 50(4), second subparagraph)

exclusions.label: Use authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences
Purely personal, non-professional use by a natural person (Art 2(10))

procedures.objective: Establish that every AI-generated or manipulated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest is either labelled clearly at the start of exposure, or qualifies for the human-review and editorial-responsibility exception, tested text by text.

testSteps.description: Define the population of published texts in the period and identify AI involvement from workflow flags and tool records; text-watermark detection may supplement, noting its lower reliability and restricted access.

Re-test the scope classification on a sample: published (open to an indeterminate audience), informing the public, on a matter of public interest; texts first published on or after 2 August 2026 count even if generated earlier.

For each sampled in-scope text: a clear label perceivable without tools (for signatories above the text, near the headline or in the colophon; partial labels allowed for AI parts), or exception evidence.

Test exception evidence: substantive human review including fact-checking or editorial control with authority to approve, alter or reject; not superficial, automated or cursory checks; editorial responsibility held and its identity and contact published.
Compare the published version with the signed-off version: any substantive AI change after sign-off voids the exception.

Inspect the editorial policy (for non-media signatories: named person with editorial responsibility, organisational measures and resources) or the existing editorial procedures of media service providers.
Evaluate accessibility of text labels (A50-P-05) and inspect the internal process and mislabel log as in A50-P-04A-S07.

criteria.members: one member per publication channel: label present or exception supported

passCriteria: A50-P-04B-C01 passes for every channel.
Exception claims are supported by substantive review, published editorial responsibility and no post-sign-off AI change.
failCriteria: A50-P-04B-C01 fails for a channel.
The exception is claimed on the basis of spell-checks, automated or cursory review, or an editorial policy that is not applied (point 135).
Editorial responsibility not identifiable publicly where the exception is relied on.
inconclusiveCriteria: Workflow records too incomplete to test the exception: limitation stated.

procedures.title: Clear, distinguishable, timely and accessible information (Art 50(5))
procedures.objective: Establish, across A50-P-01 to A50-P-04B, that the information is clear and distinguishable, reaches each person at the first interaction or exposure, and meets the accessibility requirements that apply.

testSteps.description: Determine which accessibility law applies to the product, service or content (for example the European Accessibility Act or the Web Accessibility Directive); Art 50 adds no accessibility requirement of its own.

Test the disclosure components against the applicable requirements, using EN 301 549 and WCAG 2.1 Level AA where they are the reference: text alternatives, contrast, captions and transcripts, screen-reader exposure, keyboard access.
Test 'clear and distinguishable': noticeable, understandable and separate from surrounding content; not hidden in manuals, menus or terms; for children, child-appropriate.

Test timing per person: for interactions, at least once at the start of each session for each new person; for content, for each output and each person at the first moment they are likely to perceive it, with later reminders where people may not see the start.

passCriteria: Disclosure components meet the applicable accessibility requirements and are clear, distinguishable and timely in every procedure that tested them.
failCriteria: Information hidden or easily missed under normal conditions (point 142).
A disclosure component fails an applicable accessibility requirement.
inconclusiveCriteria: The applicable accessibility law cannot be determined: LR-A50-12.

sampling.method: docs/design/audit-statistics.md (PR #46, proposed 1.0.0): Wilson interval at confidence 0.95 (z = 1.959963984540054); a member passes only when its interval lies wholly inside the band and fails only when wholly outside; a criterion passes only if every member passes; Bonferroni within a criterion for fails and across the confirmatory family; floor of 30 evaluated items per member; power checked at plan approval with the normal approximation of section 8.

methodologyDefaults.rationale: Marking is applied by deterministic pipelines, so any confirmed unmarked in-scope output is investigated as a deviation; 0.95 is a floor, raise it to 0.99 where outputs are cheap to generate (text, images).
Tests the provider's own declared reliability (Code Measure 3.2 requires it to be measured); 0.95 when nothing is declared, together with a finding that it was not declared.
False attributions harm human creators; 0.01 when nothing is declared.
The guidelines expect disclosure in all situations where the system is asked about its nature (point 40).
Conventional 5 % tolerable deviation for attribute tests; every deviation is still evaluated individually.

sampling.caveat: Internal policy. Art 50 sets no numerical marking, detection or labelling threshold, and meeting these bands is not by itself evidence of legal compliance or a presumption of conformity.

rules.label: Deterministic disclosure paths (walkthroughs)
rules.rule: Test every channel x locale x entry-point combination when there are at most 30; otherwise a documented stratified selection of at least 30 that covers every channel, every audience type and every locale meant for children or other vulnerable groups. A single failure on a deterministic path is a deviation to evaluate, not a rate.

rules.label: Marking presence per stratum (attribute sample)
rules.rule: Strata are distinct marking paths (modality x format x the channel where marking is applied separately); text also by length, with strata above the 200-token threshold. Per stratum, n from zeroFailureTable for the pre-registered band and confirmatory family size F (default 73 at F = 1). Use random production outputs where available, else a pre-registered prompt set.

rules.label: Reliability test sets
rules.rule: Positives per stratum and negatives per class (human-made; other AI systems) sized from zeroFailureTable for their bands: for example 73 positives for a 0.95 detection band and 381 negatives for a 0.01 false-positive band at F = 1. Negatives must not come from the provider's development data where avoidable.

rules.label: Robustness battery
rules.rule: At least 30 marked items per transformation (descriptive member); where a declared figure gives a band, n from zeroFailureTable or the power table for that band. Transformations and parameters are pre-registered.

rules.label: Self-identification probes
rules.rule: At least 189 probes per language stratum for the default 0.98 band at F = 1, mixing phrasing styles, persona and multi-turn contexts; agents add principal-disclosure probes.

rules.label: Deployer content and exempt-feature samples
rules.rule: Per channel stratum, at least 73 in-scope items for the default 0.95 band (all items when fewer exist); for completeness, a random sample of at least 73 unflagged items per channel screened with detectors; for exempt features, at least 73 input-output pairs per feature.

rules.label: Exposure points for Art 50(3)
rules.rule: Visit every point of exposure when there are at most 30; otherwise a documented stratified selection of at least 30 covering every site type and channel.

sampling.conclusionRule: supported: every confirmatory criterion passes, every applicable step was performed and no unresolved deviation remains; qualified: no criterion fails but at least one is inconclusive or a scope limitation applies, stated in the paper; not_supported: any criterion fails, a required element is missing, or an exception relied on is unsupported. These are the outcomes evaluateProcedure accepts.
